terms: neuron
The cell whose signals and interactions link all three biological tasks; a broad substitute would hide that common object.
fixational drift
Names the smooth movement between rapid movements; this is the measured phenomenon.
retina
Identifies the sensory tissue whose image changes during drift and gives the feedback mechanism its purpose.
place cell
A particular location-sensitive neuron; exact biological name connects the overview to the original paper.
hippocampus
Identifies the memory/navigation brain region rather than leaving place cells anatomically unplaced.
place field
A connected firing region, different from a cell and from its full map; required for later size statistics.
diffusion coefficient
D sets variance-growth units, not speed along one realized path; exact term prevents that confusion.
mean squared displacement
The observed squared-change statistic used to compare noise hypotheses; cannot be replaced with spread alone.
Brownian motion
A specific zero-mean Gaussian-increment model; the definition's continuity/variance assumptions matter to the new sum argument.
continuous attractor
Requires neutral motion along persistent states and restoring motion away; generic stable network would be wrong.
ocular motoneurons (OMNs)
Separates recorded final motor cells from proposed integrator neurons and downstream muscles.
oculomotor integrator
Identifies the stored-position circuit being proposed and tested, with movement-to-maintained-position purpose.
abducens nucleus
The anatomical recording site includes motor and other cells, so the exact site matters to classification/localization.
ocular plant
The established name for muscles plus mechanics; both roles determine the output filter.
gain
The calibration scale enabling the covariance fraction; not a vague benefit or signal amplitude.
causal filter
Specifies the present/past input restriction that makes the reconstructed spike response physical.
impulse response
The response to a unit-area spike, whose area gives calibrated gain; not merely a generic smoothing curve.
convolution
Names adding shifted input responses; the sum/integral defines what is calculated from spikes.
covariance
The shared centered product is what extracts common variance under the stated gain/noise assumptions.
correlation coefficient
Normalizes covariance by both signal standard deviations and explains why smallR need not mean smallχ.
coefficient of determination
R² is the variance removed after fitted linear rescaling, different from raw predictor squared error.
standard error of the mean (SEM)
Identifies across-cell mean uncertainty rather than cell spread or animal-level uncertainty.
p value
The null-tail probability used to assess the positive population association; exact meaning is taught locally.
low pass filter
Relative attenuation of rapid changes is the mathematical muscle-response property used in both examples.
White noise
Temporal delta covariance is the rejected input assumption; generic noisy input could include slow correlations and would widen the claim.
stationary process
Constant covariance shape in time is needed for a finite plateau; chapter expressly specifies the weaker covariance meaning.
superdiffusion
Names MSD growth faster than linear over the measured lag range, not a stronger claim of unbounded anomalous diffusion.
coefficient of variation
Dimensionless interval spread, distinguished from counting-window Fano factor and from drift amplitude.
Poisson process
The matched rate/count reference gives exponential intervals andCV1; conditional recurrent-noise scope is retained.
renewal process
Independent identical intervals justify the long-window count-CV² relation; the constant-rate condition is essential.
sub-Poisson spiking
Means lower variability than the specified matched reference; local long-window construction prevents treating allCV<1 inputs as automatically equivalent.
internal Fisher information rate
The source-derived local information-per-time scale used to compare rate and slope; exact term is taught before this application.
microsaccades
Names rapid movements removed from the fixation segments; replacing them with arbitrary eye movement would change the sample.
